title: Intercepting web proxy
description: The core web-pentest proxy: intercept, view and edit every browser request, with Intruder for brute force, Repeater, Decoder and more. https://portswigger.net/burp
output: A local proxy (127.0.0.1:8080) capturing and letting you tamper with HTTP(S) traffic.

title: Fingerprint web technologies
description: Identifies the stack behind a site: server, CMS, frameworks, JS libraries and versions.
output: Detected technologies and versions for the target URL.

title: Web content scanner
description: Dictionary-based scanner for hidden web objects and directories, analyzing each response. Simple default wordlist, good first pass.
output: Discovered paths with their status codes.

title: Web fuzzing (dirs / params)
description: Substitutes FUZZ anywhere in a request (path, params, headers, cookies); use FUZ2Z for a second marker. Hide noise with --hc/--hl/--hw/--hs (code/lines/words/string).
output: Payloads that pass your filters: hidden paths, valid params or working creds.

title: Extract JavaScript files
description: Pulls every <script> src from a page; --complete prints full URLs. Install with go install github.com/003random/getJS@latest. Grep the JS for endpoints and secrets.
output: A list of JS file URLs to grep for endpoints, API keys and comments.

title: Parse HTML comments / tags / attrs
description: tomnomnom's HTML extractor: pull comments, tag contents (tags title|script) or attributes (attribs src href). Pipe a list of URLs in. Install with go install github.com/tomnomnom/hacks/html-tool@latest.
output: Extracted comments/tags/attributes, often leaking paths, versions or dev notes.

title: Check allowed HTTP methods
description: Raw TCP connect to a web port to hand-craft requests. Send an OPTIONS request to list allowed methods; PUT/DELETE hint at WebDAV or upload paths.
output: The server's Allow: header listing enabled methods.

title: Automated SQL injection
description: Detects and exploits SQLi automatically; --dbs enumerates databases. Can dump tables/data and even run OS commands. Use -hh for the full help.
output: Confirmed injection points and the list of databases; escalate with --tables/--dump.

title: Automated command injection
description: Detects and exploits OS command injection in web parameters. Mark the injection point with INJECT_HERE (or let it find one); --cookie passes a session.
output: Command execution / a shell on the target when a parameter is injectable.

title: Automated XSS testing
description: Smart XSS scanner with payload fuzzing, context analysis and WAF detection. https://github.com/s0md3v/XSStrike
output: Reflected/DOM XSS findings with working payloads.

title: WordPress vulnerability scan
description: Scans WordPress for vulnerable plugins, themes, versions and configs. --enumerate p enumerates plugins; add --api-token for CVE data.
output: WordPress version, enumerated plugins and any known vulnerabilities.

title: Joomla vulnerability scan
description: Fingerprints the Joomla version and hunts known core/component vulnerabilities, plus extension/plugin enumeration.
output: Detected Joomla version, installed components and known weaknesses.

title: Test WebDAV upload / exec
description: Probes a WebDAV server: which file types it lets you PUT and which of those it will execute, the path to a webshell.
output: Per-extension PUT/EXEC results; an executable type that uploads is your foothold.

title: WebDAV client
description: Command-line WebDAV client: put/get/edit/move/delete files on a writable share (e.g. drop a shell after davtest confirms an executable type).
output: An interactive dav:/> prompt to upload and manage files on the server.

title: Firefox cookie editor
description: Firefox extension to view, create, edit, delete and block cookies, handy for tampering with session/auth cookies during web tests.
output: Full control over stored cookies, edit a session value and replay the request.
